9. A helium balloon is released from the floor in a room at rest, then slowly rises and comes to rest touching
   the ceiling. During this process, the gravitational potential energy of the balloon has increased. Since
   energy is conserved, the energy of something else must have decreased during this process. Which of the
   following is the main contribution to this decrease?


   (A) The kinetic energy of the balloon decreased.

   (B) The elastic potential energy of the balloon decreased.

   (C) The thermal energy of the air in the balloon decreased.

   (D) The thermal energy of the air in the room decreased.

   (E) The gravitational potential energy of the air in the room decreased.

    of water with a scale sitting on the bottom. Each of them measures the weight of their bag and rock by
    putting the bag on the scale, using three slightly different procedures.

      • Alice closes the bag carefully, so that there is no air inside.

      • Bob fills the rest of the bag with water before closing it.

      • Carol closes the bag loosely, so that it contains some air.

    (A) WC < WA < WB            (B) WA < WC < WB            (C) WA < WC = WB

    time t. At a random time, a ball is dropped from rest far above the plate, then bounces elastically off of
      it. How does the ball’s speed change during this collision?


    (A) The ball always slows down.

    (B) The ball is more likely to slow down than to speed up.

    (C) The ball is equally likely to slow down or speed up.

    (D) The ball is more likely to speed up than to slow down.

    (E) The ball always speeds up.
